problem: 'The tool electrode is a mirror shape of the cavity wanted' can mislead. The electrode is a positive replica of the cavity: the shape it has is the shape the cavity takes, not a reversed image.
fix: In die-sinking (ram EDM) the tool electrode is a positive replica of the cavity wanted, and it is sunk into the work to leave that shape as a recess.

problem: 'The cut is wider than the wire by the spark gap on each side; that extra width is the overcut' blurs radial overcut with total extra width. The quiz later uses overcut as the gap on one side (kerf = d + 2 × overcut), so the two statements look inconsistent.
fix: The cut is wider than the wire by the spark gap on each side. That one-sided gap is the overcut, so kerf width = wire diameter + 2 × overcut.

problem: E<sub>s</sub> = V<sub>g</sub> × I<sub>p</sub> × t<sub>on</sub> is only exact if voltage and current stay flat for the whole pulse. Real pulses rise and fall, so the value is an estimate.
fix: Add: this treats the pulse as a rectangular block of constant V<sub>g</sub> and I<sub>p</sub>, so E<sub>s</sub> is a good estimate, not an exact figure.

problem: 'f = 1 ÷ 200 × 10⁻⁶' read left to right gives 5 × 10⁻⁹, not 5000. The missing brackets invite a calculation slip.

'The machine can only arc or do nothing' is loose. With an insulating work plate no spark and no arc can strike at all, and the servo, seeing open-circuit gap voltage, keeps feeding the electrode down until it touches the glass.
fix: The glass does not conduct, so no spark can strike and no erosion occurs. The gap voltage stays at open circuit, so the servo keeps feeding down and the electrode simply touches the plate.
